questions.question: Define a system and describe the potential and kinetic energy in a bicycle ridden up and down a hill, and in a wind-up toy.
questions.expected_answer: A system is a set of parts that work together and transfer energy, with an input, changes and outputs. Bicycle: the rider's pedalling gives the bicycle kinetic energy; going uphill some kinetic energy changes into gravitational potential energy and it slows; going downhill potential energy changes back into kinetic energy and it speeds up; some energy is lost as heat and sound by friction. Wind-up toy: winding stores elastic potential energy in the spring; when released the spring unwinds, changing elastic potential energy into kinetic energy of the wheels.

questions.question: Explain how heating changes the kinetic energy of particles, and describe the energy changes in a gas kettle and in a coal power station.
questions.expected_answer: When a substance is heated, its particles move faster, so their kinetic energy increases; hotter objects have particles with more kinetic energy. Gas kettle: chemical potential energy in the gas is released as heat (and light) when it burns; the heat makes the water particles move faster until the water boils; some heat is lost to the air. Power station: chemical potential energy in coal is released as heat; heat boils water into high-pressure steam with kinetic energy; steam spins a turbine (kinetic energy); the turbine turns a generator, producing electrical energy; much energy is lost as heat.

questions.question: Describe how energy is stored and used in a biological system, from a plant to a person.
questions.expected_answer: Plants capture light energy from the Sun in photosynthesis and store it as chemical potential energy in sugars and starch (mealies, sugar cane, potatoes). A person (or animal) eats the food and releases the energy in cells by respiration; muscles change it into kinetic energy for movement, some becomes heat to keep the body warm, and some is stored in new tissues or as fat. In a food chain, only a small part of the energy is passed on at each step; most is used for life processes and lost as heat.
